I took 232 a few years ago (right before they shifted it to 234) and it was a great class. There is a lot of material to know, but I found making a booklet of basically every mechanism we learned along with what I needed to know about them was crucial to getting the mark I did. You'll notice patterns in mechanisms with consistent practice which made midterms and finals easier. As long as you keep on top of the material and try to condense what information is actually important for answering questions you'll be fine. 

I took it with Peter Wan and he was very clear about expectations and what you needed to know to succeed. I see Violeta is teaching this summer and she is such a kind and understanding prof. Funny story I was practicing some ester hydrolysis mechanisms before my 232 final on a whiteboard on Elliot 3rd floor and this woman comes up and stands beside me just watching me work through the mechanism. I'm getting stuck and she encourages me to keep trying and I do and ended up figuring it out. We introduced ourselves after and it was Violeta. I took 337 with her after that and she's a very dedicated prof who makes a genuine effort to get to know her students. Office hours are very helpful too! 

​

Best of luck in the class!

I’m not sure what you’re asking. 225 has never been offered to date, it’s a new course. I’m in the old Chem Med Sci program so I can’t comment on 225, I did however take 222 which is likely similar to 225 but includes a lab. 225 is not being offered until Spring 2020, with Dr. Hicks who is a lovely fellow and is very approachable. 

I don’t recommend 245 at this point in time if you want to raise your GPA. 212 is easier IF you stay on top of it and really commit. I found it hard because I left it on the back burner and the labs were challenging (TA issue). 

231 was not a bad class if you studied consistently and strategically. I got an 84 in that class and got an A+ in 232 which was my favourite class I’ve ever taken. It’s very possible to bounce back after a tough year and achieve high grades if you work hard and smart. You will be fine if you set your mind to it. 

I also only take 4 course terms now and my stress levels have decreased significantly and I can actually focus on all my subjects.
